title: Self-styled 'Godfather' gets 6 years in prison for $37 million Meta fraud scheme
summary: Adam Iza’s sentence runs concurrently with a 15-year term imposed last month for his role in an attempted bitcoin robbery.
content:
Oct 6, 2026, 8:31 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Adam Iza, 26, was sentenced to 78 months in federal prison for defrauding Meta of more than $37 million, evading taxes and using off-duty Los Angeles County sheriff’s deputies to intimidate rivals.
  • Prosecutors said Iza gained access to Meta advertising accounts and credit lines, received at least $36.4 million from the scheme and caused an estimated $13.3 million tax loss.
  • Iza was ordered to pay $23.4 million in restitution, and his sentence will run concurrently with a 15-year term for his role in an attempted Bitcoin robbery.

Adam Iza, 26, a self-styled businessman who called himself “The Godfather," was sentenced to 78 months in federal prison for defrauding Meta of more than $37 million, the U.S. Department of Justice said Tuesday.

Iza was also found guilty of evading taxes and using off-duty Los Angeles County sheriff’s deputies to intimidate people he viewed as rivals, the statement added.

U.S. District Judge Percy Anderson also ordered Iza to pay $23.4 million in restitution.

Iza pleaded guilty in January 2025 to conspiracy against rights, wire fraud and one count of tax evasion. The sentence runs concurrently with the 15-year prison term he received last month in Connecticut for his role in an attempted bitcoin robbery in August 2024.

Prosecutors said Iza gained access to Meta Business Manager accounts and associated credit lines, then sold that access to advertising companies. The Facebook parent company billed clients for ads they did not buy, then refunded them.

The case shows how crypto custodians can be used in broader fraud and tax-evasion schemes. Iza admitted moving corporate income tied to the fraud to crypto custodians while concealing his ownership of a company called Zort, according to the DOJ.

He received at least $36.4 million in income from the scheme, causing an estimated $13.3 million tax loss to the IRS, prosecutors said.

Between 2021 and 2022, Iza also hired off-duty deputies to obtain confidential law-enforcement information, personal data and search warrants to track and harass people with whom he had disputes. The five now former Los Angeles deputies involved in the scheme have since been convicted.

“Individuals with substantial financial resources must understand that they cannot purchase access to confidential databases, investigative tools, warrants, arrests, badges, or firearms for use in private disputes,” prosecutors said during sentencing, according to the DOJ statement.

A Brooklyn man was sentenced to 12 years in prison last month over a scheme involving the impersonation of Coinbase customer service representatives. Ronald Spektor deceived about 100 people, making them believe their accounts had been hacked. Las Vegas businessman Brent Kovar was found guilty in August of running a crypto Ponzi scheme. He defrauded at least 400 investors out of $24 million.

title: Hong Kong Traders Are Borrowing Like Never Before
summary:
Margin loans at Hong Kong securities brokers rose 28% in six months to HK$276.3 billion (about $35.5 billion), the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said today (Tuesday). The balance stood at HK$216.4 billion at the end of December.
The regulator's half-yearly review of the industry also showe...
content:
2026-10-06T13:57:24.157+02:00

Tuesday, 06/10/2026 | 11:57 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • About 3.7 million clients hold accounts that let them borrow to trade, two thirds of active investors.
  • The 14 largest brokers handled 21% more business but earned less in commission.

Margin loans at Hong Kong securities brokers rose 28% in six months to HK$276.3 billion (about $35.5 billion), the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said today (Tuesday). The balance stood at HK$216.4 billion at the end of December.

The regulator's half-yearly review of the industry also showed pre-tax profit at securities dealers and margin financiers rising 21% from the previous half to HK$51.7 billion, on a record HK$149.0 trillion in transactions.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Borrowing grew faster than the client base. The number of active margin clients rose 13% to about 3.71 million, against a 5% rise in cash clients to 1.97 million.

Accounts that allow borrowing now make up about two thirds of the 5.7 million active clients. Brokers' gross interest income reached HK$22.3 billion, more than the HK$20.2 billion they earned from securities commissions.

Average daily turnover on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) reached a record HK$283.0 billion, up 9.3% on the previous half, according to exchange data cited by the SFC. That followed a year in which equity turnover in Hong Kong nearly doubled.

Lending Grows as the Index Falls

The Hang Seng Index closed June at 22,881, down 11% from the end of 2025. Clients' pledged securities still covered their loans 4.7 times on average, up from 4.5 times in December, the SFC said.

Lending is concentrated. The 20 largest margin financiers held 87% of all margin loans, and brokers' own borrowings from financial institutions rose 51% in six months to HK$58.6 billion.

The SFC does not break the figures out by firm. Nasdaq-listed Futu reported a margin financing and securities lending balance of HK$95.1 billion at the end of June, up 85.1% from a year earlier.

That number, from Futu's August 20 results, covers the whole group and is not directly comparable with the regulator's data.

Eric Yip, the SFC's executive director of intermediaries, said sustaining growth would need continued work with the industry.

"We remain committed to strengthening risk management, operational resilience and conduct standards," he said.

Top Brokers Handle More Business for Less Commission

The SFC splits exchange participants into three groups by monthly turnover. Category A, the 14 largest, handled 21% more business than in the previous half, at HK$77.1 trillion, but its net securities commission income fell 9% to HK$3.2 billion.

Category A's pre-tax profit slipped 5% to HK$6.5 billion, and its proprietary trading swung to a HK$114 million loss from a HK$27 million gain.

By FinanceMagnates.com's calculation, Category A commissions equaled about 0.4 basis points of transaction value, against about 2.2 basis points for Category B and 3.5 for Category C.

Pricing pressure has also come from outside the broker ranks. ZA Bank, the city's largest digital bank, added Hong Kong stock trading last October with trading fees waived as a launch promotion.

Category B, firms ranked 15th to 65th, lifted profit 37% to HK$12.8 billion, helped by HK$3.1 billion in proprietary trading gains, up from HK$1.8 billion.

Category C profit rose 24% to HK$4.5 billion even as its transaction value fell 18%. The five largest dealers served about half of all active clients.

Crypto Dealing Commissions Drop 13.5%

Commission income from virtual asset dealing fell to HK$99.3 million from HK$114.8 million, about 0.4% of brokers' total commission income. The SFC published guidance in February allowing licensed intermediaries to finance crypto trading against collateral including bitcoin and ether.

Mainland-backed firms have taken the licensed route. Guotai Junan International was the first Chinese state-backed brokerage cleared by the SFC to deal in virtual assets, and its parent has offered to take it private.

Asset management fees across licensed firms fell 21% to HK$24.4 billion, which the SFC attributed to performance fees booked in December and not repeated in the first half.

Assets under management rose to HK$16.5 trillion from HK$14.9 trillion over the six months, and the number of licensed securities dealers and margin financiers edged up to 1,484 from 1,475.

title: Ripple Eyes Türkiye’s $200B Crypto Market as RLUSD and Bank Custody Gain Ground
summary:
Key Takeaways: Retail trading is estimated to have reached approximately $40 billion in early 2026 and crypto transaction volume has exceeded $200 billion in a year in Türkiye. Ripple continues
The post Ripple Eyes Türkiye’s $200B Crypto Market as RLUSD and Bank Custody Gain Ground appeared first on...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Retail trading is estimated to have reached approximately $40 billion in early 2026 and crypto transaction volume has exceeded $200 billion in a year in Türkiye.
  • Ripple continues to build on its local footprint by developing its infrastructure and dollar-backed stablecoin, RLUSD.
  • Garanti BBVA Kripto has partnerships with Ripple Custody, platforms like BiLira and Bitlo have partnerships with RLUSD.

Türkiye is becoming one of the most dynamic digital asset markets in the world, while ongoing risks to the lira are helping it venture further away from retail speculation into the crypto market.

Ripple is zeroing in on that transition as banks, exchanges and businesses are looking for regulated infrastructure to keep digital assets and the dollar safe.

  • Türkiye’s Crypto Market Approaches $200 Billion
  • Ripple Expands Custody Through Garanti BBVA Kripto
    • RLUSD Adds a Dollar-Linked Option

Türkiye’s Crypto Market Approaches $200 Billion

Total volume of crypto transactions in Turkey has reached $200 billion a year, with crypto inflows of approximately $878 billion since 2021 and up to mid-2025.

Retail activity also remains strong. As the early 2026 data shows, trading volume surged by 7% year on year to around $40 billion placing Türkiye in the top five countries for crypto adoption in a submerged global ranking. The market is seeking to go beyond the individual trader, however.

Digital assets are being adopted by businesses and financial institutions for actual financial transactions as pressure on the dollar currency grows and liquidity remains constrained.

As a result of that environment, there is a more pressing need for investing in stable coins, like Ripple USD, or RLUSD.

Read More: Ripple Launches Ripple Mint, Unlocking Scalable RLUSD Access for Global Institutions

Ripple Expands Custody Through Garanti BBVA Kripto

Crypto regulations became much stricter in Türkiye since 2024. Regulatory authority over cryptocurrencies was assigned to the Capital Markets Board (CMB) by Law No. 7518, and subsidiary rules were included in March 2025 and provided the regulatory framework for crypto asset service providers as well as licensing, capital and anti-money laundering requirements.

In addition, further custody conditions were established by the extension of the restrictions in 2026 to solidify the regulatory framework for digital asset companies in the nation. Ripple has taken advantage of that change to further expand its institutional penetration.

Garanti BBVA Kripto, digital asset subsidiary of Garanti BBVA, utilizes Ripple Yard, the solutions supplier, to service its Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP operations. Following its successful pilot in 2023, the service was rolled out to the bank’s customers later that year.

Read More: Ripple Prime Secures $275M Funding Boost to Power Its Expanding U.S. Crypto Business

RLUSD Adds a Dollar-Linked Option

Another opportunity for Ripple’s stabilization is with regular distribution of the stablecoins. The Turkish platforms Bilira and Bitlo are offering to institutions and users this asset, the dolhardollar, in the era when the demand for dollar-backed liquidity is increasing.

The shift is particularly important as retail investors turned to cryptocurrencies as a viable alternative when the lira has not been able to withstand the inflationary pressures.

Digital asset services are now expanding as banks and financial companies sense more assurance in the certification. Ripple has identified Türkiye as a potential market for their custody, compliance and stablecoin solutions, in addition to a country with high levels of crypto adoption.

Are bitcoin BTC$83,886.55 and U.S. stocks truly calm and poised for more gains, or is this the calm before the storm? That is the question some macro observers are asking.

They point to rising volatility in Treasury notes, which underpin global finance, as an early sign of stress that usually spills over into other markets with a lag.

“The MOVE index is making higher lows while the VIX makes lower highs. The MOVE leads: it flashed turbulence before the VIX in 2022, in 2023, and at the start of the Iran war. Stocks are usually the last to get the message,” Kurt S. Altrichter, wealth manager and writer of the RiskSIGNAL Report, said.

The MOVE Index, officially the ICE BofA U.S. Bond Market Option Volatility Estimate, is the bond market’s version of the VIX. It gauges how much U.S. Treasury yields are expected to swing over the next month, using options on 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year bonds, with the 10-year given the heaviest weight. In plain terms, it tells us how much movement traders are pricing into Treasury yields over the next month, without saying whether yields will go up or down.

Because Treasury notes are preferred collateral in international finance and affect almost all kinds of borrowing costs in the economy, a rising volatility in these instruments can cause global financial tightening, push up risk premiums, and trigger broad-based risk aversion.

Lately, the index has been on the rise. It jumped 46% in June and is hovering around 116, close to its March high and the loftiest reading since April 2025.

The upswing in MOVE is already affecting corporate borrowing.

“Corporate bond volatilities have both continued to climb with investment grade (IG) and high-yield (HY) vols jumping from 6th and 11th percentile lows 2 weeks ago to their 79th and 84th percentile highs respectively,” Cboe said on X.

Bitcoin’s daily returns don’t track the MOVE Index closely over 60- or 90-day windows, according to data analyzed by CoinDesk. Even so, analysts have told CoinDesk previously that sudden jumps in Treasury volatility can hurt bitcoin, with the magnitude of moves in bonds mattering more than whether yields rise or fall.

So, traders may want to watch for a potential spike in bitcoin and S&P 500 volatility, especially if the MOVE Index clears its March high. For now, BTC’s 30-day implied volatility gauge (BVIV) and the S&P 500’s VIX are hovering near year-to-date lows.

For now, steady ETF inflows, fewer whale deposits to exchanges, and supportive regulatory tailwinds underpin the bull case. Stay alert.

Read more: For analysis of today's activity in altcoins and derivatives, see Crypto Markets Today. For a comprehensive list of events this week, see CoinDesk's Crypto Week Ahead.

What’s trending

  • U.S. scraps proposed $10,000 reporting rule for for crypto sent to private wallets (CoinDesk): The Treasury Department scrapped a years-old proposal that would have forced banks and crypto businesses to collect and report more information when customers sent large amounts of crypto to wallets they controlled themselves.
  • Why bitcoin is down 'just' 32% a year after its record high of $126,000 (CoinDesk): A year after hitting a record high above $126,000 on Oct. 6, 2025, bitcoin is down just 32%, at $85,453. Essentially, two things have changed. The bear market has been shallower, and its worst point arrived earlier.
  • Stocks climb, yields retreat from multi-decade highs (Reuters): European stocks rose on Tuesday, extending a global equity rally as investors turned more optimistic ahead of earnings season, while easing pressure ​in longer-dated bonds and lower oil prices helped calm markets.
  • Nvidia heads for $6 trillion value with chipmaker back at record (Bloomberg): Nvidia Corp. is on the verge of becoming the first company with a $6 trillion market capitalization as investors rotate back into the artificial-intelligence chipmaker.

Today’s signal

The chart shows daily swings in the MOVE index.

It’s close to topping its March high of 115 points. The next resistance is seen directly at 140, the high registered in early April when escalating trade tensions between the U.S. and China rocked global markets.

title: Sui (SUI) Price Prediction: SUI Is Trapped Near $1.20—Analyst Flags $1.35 as the Key Breakout Level
summary: Sui (SUI) is consolidating around $1.20 after a sharp recovery from its 2026 lows, with traders watching $1.35 as a potential technical breakout level.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: SUI

Sui (SUI) is consolidating around $1.20 after a sharp recovery from its 2026 lows, with traders watching $1.35 as a potential technical breakout level.

The SUI price remains below recent highs near $1.25, leaving the token caught between immediate resistance and support around the $1.15–$1.18 area. Several TradingView analyses point to a possible structural shift if buyers can clear the upper levels with confirmation.

SUI Price Holds Near $1.20 as Resistance Tightens

SUI has been trading within a relatively narrow range after recovering from levels near $0.64 earlier in the year. Recent price action has brought the SUI crypto asset back toward the $1.20–$1.25 region, where sellers have repeatedly limited upside.

SUI is trading within a well-defined 4H range, with support near $1.139 and resistance at $1.192–$1.205. Source: Donatelio on TradingView

A TradingView analysis by Donatelio identifies $1.139 as nearby support and $1.192–$1.205 as the immediate resistance zone. The analyst noted that buyers have been active during pullbacks but have so far struggled to maintain prices above $1.20.

The setup leaves the price at an important short-term decision point. A sustained move above $1.205 could expose $1.27 and then $1.309, according to the analysis. Conversely, a break below $1.139 followed by a failed recovery could return attention to the $1.05–$1.09 area.

The analyst described the market as a range and said a confirmed break in either direction would provide a clearer signal than trading inside the current consolidation.

$1.35 Emerges as the Key SUI Breakout Level

Another TradingView contributor sees a more constructive structure on the four-hour chart. The analysis points to successive bullish market-structure breaks and notes that buyers defended the $1.10–$1.15 region during the latest pullback.

A 4H close above $1.30–$1.35 and a successful retest could signal further upside toward $1.50, $1.65, and $1.90–$2.00. Source: Alawan11 on TradingView

Rather than fully retracing the preceding advance, SUI has remained around $1.20–$1.25. The analyst characterized this consolidation as potentially constructive because the token has held relatively close to its recent highs.

The key level in that analysis is $1.35. A four-hour close above the $1.30–$1.35 resistance area, followed by a successful retest, would provide stronger technical confirmation of a continuation move.

The analyst wrote that the “real confirmation” would come from a clean break and retest of $1.35. The same analysis places potential upside levels around $1.50, $1.65, and $1.90–$2.00 if that resistance is decisively overcome.

At the same time, the setup has clear downside levels. A loss of $1.15 would weaken the bullish structure, while a decisive move below $1.05 could shift attention back toward the $0.94 area.

Long-Term SUI Chart Faces Descending Trendline

The broader SUI chart presents a more complicated picture. A TradingView analysis by CryptoNuclear shows the token approaching a descending trendline that has acted as resistance since prices were around $4.40.

SUI is currently retesting a long-term descending trendline that has been acting as resistance since the area around $4.40. Source: CryptoNuclear on TradingView

SUI’s recovery from approximately $0.64 has brought the price back toward this long-term barrier. This makes the current area important beyond the shorter four-hour range.

The analysis cautions that the broader structure cannot be considered bullish until the price breaks the descending trendline and holds above it. A confirmed two-day candle close over the trendline would provide stronger evidence that the long-term downtrend is losing momentum.

That distinction is important for the current SUI price prediction. A move above $1.35 would represent a significant technical development, but it would not by itself eliminate all longer-term resistance.

The same analysis identifies $1.332 as an initial resistance zone, followed by $1.49, $1.65, and $1.895. Further levels are placed around $2.165 and $2.62 if a sustained breakout develops.

SUI Technical Indicators Remain Mixed

Short-term technical indicators do not yet provide a uniformly bullish signal. Data referenced in the source material shows the 14-period Relative Strength Index near 43, below the neutral 50 threshold.

SUI price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Other oscillators also lean toward caution. The Stochastic indicator was around 25, while the MACD remained slightly negative. Williams %R and the Ultimate Oscillator similarly pointed to selling pressure. At the same time, Stochastic RSI was near an oversold reading, suggesting that short-term weakness had already pushed momentum toward the lower end of its recent range.

Moving averages show a similar split. SUI was trading below several shorter-period averages, including the 10-, 20-, and 50-period measures. Longer-term averages were more supportive, with the 100- and 200-period levels providing potential dynamic support.

This divergence helps explain why the SUI crypto price remains sensitive to the $1.15–$1.20 area. Shorter-term momentum is cautious, while the broader recovery has not yet broken down.

SUI Price Prediction: Key Levels to Watch

The current technical structure gives traders several reference points rather than a single directional signal.

On the upside, $1.20–$1.25 remains the first resistance area, followed by $1.30–$1.35. A confirmed break above $1.35 would strengthen the bullish case and put $1.50 and $1.65 on the chart.

SUI established a $0.9446–$3.0166 range, with the low taken on Feb. 2, 2026, before retesting and forming local extremes at $0.7893 and $1.4125. Source: Kenanie on TradingView

Beyond those levels, the longer-term analysis identifies $1.895, $2.165, and potentially $2.62 as additional resistance zones. These should be viewed as technical reference points rather than forecasts of where SUI must trade.

On the downside, $1.15–$1.18 is an important near-term support area. Below that, $1.05–$1.10 becomes the next zone to monitor, followed by approximately $0.94.

One TradingView analyst also identified $0.9446 as the lower boundary of a larger trading range extending toward $3.0166. In that framework, a move back toward the range high would require a much broader change in market structure.

SUI Outlook Depends on Confirmation

SUI is currently positioned between a recovering longer-term structure and unresolved resistance. The token’s ability to remain above the $1.15–$1.18 support zone could keep the recent bullish structure intact, but the market has yet to confirm a decisive breakout.

The $1.20 area remains an immediate battleground. A sustained move above $1.205 could open the door toward $1.27 and $1.309, while the more significant $1.30–$1.35 region remains the key test for the broader bullish setup.

A confirmed break and retest above $1.35 would strengthen the case for higher technical levels, including $1.50 and $1.65. Until that happens, SUI remains in consolidation, with both bullish continuation and renewed downside still possible.

For now, the SUI price prediction hinges less on a specific target and more on confirmation. Holding support would preserve the recovery structure, while a clean breakout above $1.35 would provide a clearer signal that buyers are gaining control.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin remains locked in range as stocks notch another new record high
summary: FxPro says a slide below $84,000 would hand control to sellers and put $80,000 in play. Minutes from the Fed's last meeting come out Wednesday.
content:
coverage endedOct 6, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT

FxPro says a slide below $84,000 would hand control to sellers and put $80,000 in play. Minutes from the Fed's last meeting come out Wednesday.

Nasdaq and S&P 500 close at record highs

The gains were modest — the Nasdaq rising 0.5% and the S&P 500 0.6% — but it was enough for the two major U.S. stock indexes to close at new record highs.

While the Nasdaq has been making new highs regularly, it was the S&P’s first all-time close in two months.

The Mag 7 names were broadly higher, though Meta slipped a hair. There was also strength in recently beaten-down consumer names and utilities as interest rates took a rare move lower.

Crypto prices continued their recent flatlining action, with bitcoin, ether, XRP, and solana all little changed over the past 24 hours.

'Coping' as bitcoin continues to flatline

“‘The longer the base, the higher the space’ is the appropriate cope while waiting for bitcoin’s next range breakout,” writes Brian Brookshire.

Brookshire writes as bitcoin at $85,500 continues to trade in a narrow range for about the fourth consecutive week.

Bulls might recall that the price action since mid-September resembles that of this past summer, when bitcoin traded similarly, but in the low- to mid-$60,000 area.

Kalshi moves into U.S. equities with stock index perpetual future

Prediction market platform Kalshi has launched a stock index perpetual future, adding to growing competition for perps in the U.S.

The US 500 perpetual tracks an index of large U.S. companies and lets traders bet on the market rising or falling without an expiration date. That means traders don't have to roll their positions into new contracts, as they do with traditional futures.

The launch is Kalshi's first move into equity markets as the company expands beyond its core prediction-market business. Kalshi, which is regulated by the CFTC, launched perpetual futures tied to cryptocurrencies in May.

Winklevoss brothers file for Zcash ETF

Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, who came to fame through their involvement in the creation of Facebook and later started crypto exchange Gemini, have filed for an exchange-traded fund (ETF) tracking Zcash.

The brothers, through their firm Winklevoss Asset Services, submitted a S-1 registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Tuesday. The ETF would hold the crypto directly and trade on Nasdaq under the ticker WINK, according to the filing.

The fund would be custodied by Gemini, the crypto exchange led by the two brothers.

Morgan Stanley says Wall Street could capture much of the value from crypto’s growth

Wall Street firms could emerge as major winners as crypto technology moves deeper into finance, according to Morgan Stanley.

The bank argues that traditional financial institutions can adopt blockchain technology while retaining much of the economic value because they already control distribution, client relationships, balance sheets and regulated market infrastructure. Morgan Stanley expects digital assets to become part of the existing financial system rather than replace it.

That shift could accelerate as markets move toward round-the-clock trading. Morgan Stanley says 24/7 tokenized securities will also need digital cash and collateral that can move outside banking hours, creating a larger role for stablecoins and tokenized funds.

The transition could also reshape competition among blockchains. Ethereum ETH$2,614.90 and Solana (SOL) have large existing ecosystems, but Morgan Stanley says institutional adoption could favor networks that offer privacy, identity controls and regulatory compliance, pointing to Canton as one example.

“End clients may ultimately use blockchain infrastructure without experiencing the product as ‘crypto,’” Morgan Stanley said.

Bullish analyst reiterates lofty price target for Hut 8 after River Bend event

Hut 8 HUT$92.20·Market Closed yesterday opened its River Bend project in West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana to analysts and investors.

Among them was StoneX’s Mark Palmer, who said the project highlights two Hut 8 competitive advantages: 1) The ability to build in partnership with communities at a time of resistance to AI data centers, and 2) “Speed to power,” i.e., delivering to customers (in this case, Anthropic) on schedule and on budget.

Palmer reiterated his buy rating and $195 price target, or more than 100% upside from the current $89.

Marvell shares jump 8% as chipmaker raises revenue outlook

Shares of Marvell (MRVL), which designs data-center networking and AI chips, rose 8% to $292 after the company projected annual revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion by fiscal 2031 and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to $20 billion from around $18 billion. The stock now trades just 12% below its all-time high after dropping as much as 50% from the June all-time high.

Bitcoin rises modestly as S&P hits record high

The S&P 500 is up 0.6% early Tuesday to 7,821, notching its first record high since August.

Tech and healthcare are leading, while the energy sector dips alongside oil dropping to its lowest level since late August.

Bitcoin BTC$83,886.55 — now on the one-year anniversary of last reaching a record — is catching the smallest of bids, rising to a session high of $86,400.

Crude oil slumps to weakest level since the summer

WTI crude oil for November delivery is lower by 2.3% to $87.36 per barrel, its weakest price since late August. Earlier Tuesday, it had fallen back to $86.88.

Diesel fuel (heating oil) is down similarly, and at $4.41 per gallon is down 15% after hitting a record high about three weeks ago.

There’s no particular good news out of the Middle East, but there’s also no bad news.

That’s giving some support to the bond market, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield down 4 basis points to 5.27%. Risk markets are higher, led by Nasdaq 100 futures higher by 0.6%.

Crypto is higher from late Monday lows, but the majors are about flat over the past 24 hours.

'Le Spread' narrows as leading French presidential candidate promises fiscal reform

The yield spread between French 10-year OATS and German 10-year Bunds — colloquially known as “Le Spread” — has narrowed more than 10 basis points on Tuesday to 125 basis points. Just days ago, the spread had spiked to 160 basis points, suggesting another EU debt crisis might be at hand.

Her party leading in the polls, presidential hopeful Marine Le Pen proposed a plan to narrow France’s government budget deficit to 3.7% of GDP next year and 2.2% by 2032 — both well below the targeted 5%.

In absolute terms, the yield on French 10-year paper is down 13 basis points to 4.73%, while German yields are lower by 2 basis points.

“Note that this is a shadow budget, so in effect what she would propose if her party was in power,” said UBS’s Nana Antiedu. “Assuming Le Pen's party were to win the 2027 presidential election and go through the legal process of changing the budget, a deficit of 3% by 2032 is quite ambitious, and would require her to gain agreement from the other parties.”

Tech stocks continue to set records

Tech stocks continue to set records, with Invesco QQQ rising another 0.5% to an all-time high of $760. Nvidia NVDA$239.22·Market Closed also reached a record $241 per share in premarket trading on Tuesday.

A modest retreat in bond yields, the dollar and oil prices is supporting risk appetite. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield fell to 5.258%, while the dollar index slipped below 102 and WTI crude dropped back to $87 a barrel.

Bitcoin climbed above $86,000, while gold gained almost 1% to trade just below $4,200 an ounce.

A drop below $84,000 would put $80,000 in play for bitcoin

Bitcoin traded just above $86,000 early Tuesday, down 0.2% over 24 hours. On Monday it pushed above $87,000 and ran into heavy selling for the third time since Sept. 23.

ZEC led the majors with a gain of nearly 2% to about $1,360. DOGE was the laggard, down nearly 2%. SOL fell 1%, and ether, XRP and BNB each slipped less than 1%, CoinDesk data shows.

According to FxPro, bitcoin briefly slid to $85,200 before European trading opened. It's still near the top of the range it has traded in for the past two weeks. The run of higher lows that began at the start of last week is under threat, the firm said, but hasn't broken yet.

"A break below $84K would signal a victory for the bears," FxPro said, meaning traders betting on lower prices would have the upper hand. A further fall through the recent low near $83,000 would confirm that shift and could send bitcoin to $80,000 fairly quickly, according to the firm.

Bonds offered some relief. U.S. Treasury yields fell from their highest since 2002 as oil slipped below $100 a barrel. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also said economic growth and spending restraint would "very quickly" start to slow government borrowing. That paused a global bond selloff driven by inflation fears tied to the U.S.-Iran war and bets that the Fed will keep tightening.

Minutes from the Fed's last meeting come out Wednesday.

title: Smaller altcoins shine as bitcoin stills trades around $85,000
summary: Leading the gains is BTW, the native token of Bitway, a bitcoin-compatible layer-1, which jumped 25% in the past 24 hours and is up 170% over the past 30 days.
content:
3 min pagbasa

Buod

  • Bitway’s BTW token rose 25 percent in 24 hours and 170 percent over the past month, leading a broader rally among smaller cryptocurrencies.
  • Bitcoin traded near $85,900, with analysts warning that a drop below $84,000 could open the way for a swift decline toward $80,000.
  • Bitcoin derivatives positioning stabilized as open interest held near $21.9 billion, funding rates cooled and 24-hour liquidations reached $163 million.

Smaller coins are stealing the spotlight again as bitcoin BTC$83,874.11, ether ETH$2,615.51 and other major cryptocurrencies are still trading in a choppy range, while

Leading the gains is BTW, the native token of Bitway, a bitcoin-compatible layer-1 blockchain with proof-of-stake consensus and decentralized finance (DeFi) infrastructure. The token has jumped 25% in the past 24 hours and is up 170% over the past 30 days.

BTW has also been drawing attention on social media, following the end of Binance Wallet's "Booster Season 5" campaign on Oct. 2. The campaign offered rewards for deposits and may have boosted retail engagement.

The rally also appears to be part of a broader shift toward smaller altcoins. Filecoin's FIL and LayerZero's ZRO have gained 12% and 10%, respectively, in 24 hours, and both are up 50% or more over four weeks. Midnight's NIGHT token has added 8% over the same 24 hours.

At the other end, SKY, VVV and DASH are the three worst performers among the 100 largest tokens by market value.

As for bitcoin, it remains stuck in its range. The leading cryptocurrency is trading at $85,900 as of this writing, after putting in lows near $85,000 earlier in the day.

"A break below $84K would signal a victory for the bears, and a break below the recent local lows at $83K would confirm this with even greater certainty. In this scenario, the leading cryptocurrency could fall to $80K fairly quickly," said Alex Kuptsikevich, chief market analyst at TheFxPro.

Derivatives positioning

  • BTC open interest held roughly flat at $21.9B (from $22.0B), while funding rates cooled a touch - now broadly 0–5% annualized across venues, down from the elevated 4–10% range. The 3-month annualized basis held steady in the 5–6% range. Positioning is stabilising after Friday's build: leveraged longs still in place, but the heat is coming off funding.
  • Options flow stayed call-skewed, the 24-hour put/call volume ratio at 62/38 in favour of calls. The 1-week 25-delta skew remains negative at ~-2%, and the ATM term structure is unchanged - still in contango, front end ~24–25% rising to ~39% by late 2027
  • Coinglass data shows $163M in 24 hour liquidations, with a 63-27 split between longs and shorts. BTC ($51M), Others ($21M) and ETH ($19M) were the leaders in terms of notional liquidations. Binance liquidation heatmap indicates $87,150 as a core liquidation level to monitor, in case of a price rise.

Token talk

  • Privacy tokens bucked wider weakness to lead the day's gains, with Monero (XMR) advancing 1.9% to $557 and Zcash (ZEC) gaining 2.5% to cross back above $1,350 as demand for anonymous layer-1 assets remains firm amid shifting macro sentiment.
  • Near protocol NEAR$4.9740 was among the standout performers in the altcoin space, jumping 4.5% over 24 hours to trade at $5.25 as buying interest returned following last week's sharp market-wide pullback.
  • Rain protocol RAIN$0.01124 led today’s decliners, falling 5.6% as selling pressure resumed following recent supply emissions and broader profit-taking across speculative low-cap altcoins.
  • Large-cap DeFi standard-bearers traded slightly lower, with Uniswap (UNI) slipping 1.4% to $8.89 and Chainlink LINK$13.55 easing 1.2% to $14, reflecting quiet, range-bound consolidation across decentralized finance protocols.
  • Sui SUI$1.1376 gave back recent gains, dropping 3.2% over 24 hours to trade near $1.20 as the layer-1 token continues to digest its recent multi-session volatility.

title: Crypto Licensing Enters a New Era as Global Regulations Accelerate in 2026
summary:
The global digital asset industry is entering a defining chapter as governments and financial regulators continue to introduce comprehensive frameworks for crypto licensing. After years of uncertainty, many jurisdictions are
The post Crypto Licensing Enters a New Era as Global Regulations Accelerate...
content:
The global digital asset industry is entering a defining chapter as governments and financial regulators continue to introduce comprehensive frameworks for crypto licensing. After years of uncertainty, many jurisdictions are shifting away from fragmented oversight toward structured authorization systems designed to improve transparency, strengthen consumer protection, and support sustainable market growth.

Throughout 2026, crypto licensing has become one of the most discussed topics among blockchain companies, fintech startups, institutional investors, and compliance professionals. Rather than treating regulation as a barrier, an increasing number of businesses now view licensing as a competitive advantage that enables international expansion and builds long-term trust with customers.

  • Regulation Is Moving from Guidance to Enforcement
  • Europe Continues to Set the Pace
  • More Jurisdictions Compete to Attract Digital Asset Businesses
  • Institutional Investors Prefer Licensed Platforms
  • Compliance Technology Is Becoming Essential
  • Licensing Influences Customer Trust
  • Challenges Remain for Smaller Businesses
  • The Future of Crypto Licensing

Regulation Is Moving from Guidance to Enforcement

The regulatory landscape has changed dramatically over the past few years. Authorities that once relied primarily on general financial legislation are now introducing dedicated licensing regimes specifically designed for digital asset service providers.

This transition reflects the growing maturity of the industry. As crypto-related services become integrated into payment systems, investment platforms, and digital commerce, regulators are demanding higher operational standards from companies that manage customer assets or facilitate digital transactions.

Businesses entering the market today are expected to demonstrate more than innovative technology. Licensing applications increasingly require detailed governance structures, risk management policies, cybersecurity frameworks, anti-money laundering procedures, and ongoing compliance programs.

The result is a more professional ecosystem where licensed companies are better positioned to attract institutional partnerships and operate across multiple jurisdictions.

Europe Continues to Set the Pace

Europe remains one of the most influential regions in shaping the future of crypto licensing.

The implementation of harmonized regulatory standards across European markets is encouraging companies to rethink their licensing strategies. Instead of maintaining separate compliance approaches for different countries, many organizations are preparing for broader operational frameworks that allow them to serve multiple markets under consistent regulatory expectations.

This shift has created significant demand for legal advisors, compliance specialists, technology providers, and licensing consultants capable of guiding businesses through increasingly sophisticated authorization processes.

Industry experts note that obtaining a license is no longer viewed as the final objective. Maintaining ongoing compliance has become equally important, requiring regular reporting, internal audits, employee training, and continuous monitoring of regulatory updates.

More Jurisdictions Compete to Attract Digital Asset Businesses

While Europe remains a major regulatory hub, competition among international jurisdictions continues to intensify.

Countries across Asia, the Middle East, North America, and offshore financial centers are refining their licensing frameworks to attract responsible digital asset businesses while maintaining high compliance standards.

Many regulators are balancing two important objectives:

  • Encouraging innovation within financial technology.
  • Preventing financial crime and protecting consumers.

This balance has resulted in licensing models that differ in complexity, capital requirements, reporting obligations, and supervisory expectations.

For businesses planning international expansion, selecting the right licensing jurisdiction has become a strategic business decision rather than simply a legal requirement.

Institutional Investors Prefer Licensed Platforms

One of the strongest trends observed during 2026 is the growing preference of institutional investors for licensed crypto businesses.

Banks, venture capital firms, payment providers, and financial institutions increasingly evaluate regulatory status before establishing commercial relationships with crypto companies.

A recognized license demonstrates that a business has undergone regulatory scrutiny and operates within defined legal standards. Although licensing does not eliminate operational risk, it significantly improves credibility and provides additional confidence to partners and customers alike.

This trend is encouraging even early-stage blockchain startups to prioritize licensing much earlier in their development cycle than was common just a few years ago.

Compliance Technology Is Becoming Essential

As regulatory obligations become more sophisticated, technology is playing an increasingly important role in helping licensed companies remain compliant.

Modern compliance solutions now automate many previously manual processes, including customer verification, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, suspicious activity detection, document management, and regulatory reporting.

Artificial intelligence is also beginning to assist compliance teams by identifying unusual transaction patterns, improving fraud detection, and reducing false-positive alerts.

These technological improvements allow licensed businesses to manage growing regulatory responsibilities more efficiently while maintaining operational scalability.

Licensing Influences Customer Trust

Consumer expectations have also evolved considerably.

Retail and institutional users alike are paying closer attention to whether a platform operates under regulatory supervision before depositing funds or using digital asset services.

Market participants increasingly associate licensing with transparency, accountability, and stronger operational controls.

Although no regulatory framework can completely eliminate business risk, licensed providers generally offer greater visibility regarding governance, complaint handling, compliance practices, and customer protection mechanisms.

For many businesses, displaying licensing credentials has become an important component of their overall brand strategy.

Challenges Remain for Smaller Businesses

Despite the positive momentum, obtaining a crypto license continues to present significant challenges, particularly for startups and smaller technology companies.

Application procedures often require extensive documentation, experienced compliance personnel, legal expertise, and ongoing financial commitments.

In addition to initial licensing costs, companies must prepare for continuous regulatory supervision, periodic reporting, independent audits, and evolving compliance obligations.

These requirements may increase operational expenses, but many industry observers argue that stronger regulation ultimately contributes to a healthier and more sustainable market by discouraging fraudulent operators and encouraging responsible business practices.

The Future of Crypto Licensing

Looking ahead, industry analysts expect crypto licensing to become even more interconnected across international markets.

Greater cooperation between financial regulators may simplify cross-border supervision while improving information sharing related to financial crime prevention and consumer protection.

Emerging technologies such as tokenized financial instruments, decentralized finance integrations, stablecoin ecosystems, and blockchain-based payment infrastructures are also expected to influence future licensing requirements.

Rather than slowing innovation, modern regulatory frameworks are increasingly being designed to support responsible growth while maintaining market integrity.

Companies that invest early in governance, compliance, and licensing are likely to benefit from stronger business relationships, improved customer confidence, and greater access to international opportunities.

Crypto licensing is no longer viewed as a niche regulatory requirement reserved for large financial institutions. It has become a central pillar of the digital asset industry and an essential element of long-term business strategy.

As governments continue refining regulatory frameworks throughout 2026, licensed businesses are expected to enjoy greater credibility, stronger institutional partnerships, and improved opportunities for global expansion.

For companies operating in the rapidly evolving blockchain economy, compliance is increasingly becoming more than a legal obligation; it is a foundation for sustainable growth, investor confidence, and long-term success.

The differences between NFT gaming sites vs traditional play hubs are anonymity and privacy, supported currencies, access, rewards, transaction speed, and security. While traditional online gaming hubs often require identity verification and personal details, NFT entertainment systems usually allow players to participate using just a crypto wallet, offering a more private experience.

Regarding supported currencies, NFT/crypto predicting sites rely on digital assets, whereas traditional entertainment platforms primarily operate with fiat currencies. In terms of access, NFT gaming sites are usually open to anyone with an internet connection and a crypto wallet, as long as the platform you choose is not restricted in your region.

Thanks to blockchain technology, transaction speed is faster on NFT gaming platforms, enabling near-instant deposits and withdrawals. In contrast, traditional gaming transactions can be slower due to banking processes.

Lastly, NFT entertained sites operate on decentralized systems, offering transparent smart contracts and provably fair games, while traditional sites rely on centralized systems that require trust in the house’s fairness.

How to Choose the Best NFT Gaming Sites to Play?

Before using any NFT-linked platform, assess it against factors that affect user protection more than promotional appeal: licensing and regulation, game structure, supported assets, promotional terms, security, user experience, and transaction costs.

  2. Game Variety: Look for platforms offering a wide range of games, including slots, live games, table games, and NFT-specific games. Top sites like Mega Dice and BC.Game offers thousands of titles from leading software providers, ensuring quality and diversity.
  3. Supported Cryptocurrencies and NFTs: Choose NFT sites that support multiple cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin, USDC, etc.) and allow you to use, earn, or trade NFTs easily.
  4. Bonuses and Promotions: Evaluate welcome bonuses, free spins, reloads, cashback, and ongoing promotions. Some NFT hubs offer generous packages, but check the wagering requirements and fairness of terms.
  5. Security and Privacy: Ensure the site uses strong encryption and privacy measures. NFT sites often allow anonymous play with crypto wallets, reducing the need for personal data submission. The best NFT platforms should have secure NFT wallet integration like MetaMask, Coinbase, Binance, or eToro.
  6. User Experience: A smooth, intuitive interface enhances gameplay. Some sites may have cluttered layouts due to many offerings, so choose one that balances features with ease of use.

title: HSBC RedCoin Targets 74% Stablecoin-Aware Users Ahead of Hong Kong Launch
summary:
Key Takeaways: HSBC has officially unveiled the name of its stablecoin, HSBC RedCoin Of the 1,060 consumers surveyed, 74% now understand at least one use case for stablecoins, indicating rising

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • HSBC has officially unveiled the name of its stablecoin, HSBC RedCoin
  • Of the 1,060 consumers surveyed, 74% now understand at least one use case for stablecoins, indicating rising consumer awareness
  • Limited to P2P transfers and merchant transactions initially, further institutional applications will follow

HSBC has unveiled the official name of its forthcoming Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin, HSBC RedCoin, marking a significant step in the bank’s digital asset strategy. The announcement comes alongside new survey data showing strong interest in stablecoins among Hong Kong consumers, even as concerns around regulation and security remain.

  • HSBC Introduces RedCoin Ahead of Stablecoin Launch
  • Survey Reveals Strong Stablecoin Awareness
    • Knowledge Gaps Still Exist
    • Security and Regulation Remain Top Priorities
    • RedCoin Begins with Retail Payments

HSBC Introduces RedCoin Ahead of Stablecoin Launch

The upcoming HSBC dollar stablecoin will be called HSBC RedCoin owing the brand name of the Bank and its enduring presence in Hong Kong, the bank confirmed.

The stablecoin has not been made available yet. The token will be released under a stablecoins licence issued earlier this year by HSBC and will be introduced in the second half of 2026. The initial rollout will be to the PayMe platform and the HSBC HK Mobile App.

HSBC says they will take first cut at the basic payment features in the initial phase. The app will also enable users to transfer funds among themselves and pay merchants with the stablecoin. Later in the stages it is thought that more advanced use cases involving corporate and institutional transactions will emerge.

Bruce Maggie Ng, the CEO of HSBC Hong Kong, said that launching the new offering is a part of the bank’s strategy to enable financial innovation while retaining the trust and security of traditional financial institutions.

Read More: BlackRock, JPMorgan, Coinbase Join UK Tokenization Taskforce Targeting $88T RWA Market

Survey Reveals Strong Stablecoin Awareness

The naming came with a study surveying 1,060 HSBC customers aged 18 to 64. 74% of respondents noted they could see at least one practical use for stablecoins, the results indicated. The most popular were person-to-person transfers with 0.53% and digital asset trading at 0.57%.

Both cross-border remittances paced at 52% showed that stablecoins are also becoming a means of payment for consumers, not just a speculative investment.

Knowledge Gaps Still Exist

Yet misconceptions were discovered with the survey even after increased awareness. 26% identified a stablecoin as a fiat-issued digital asset, though 60% did. The other 10% believed that stablecoins do this naturally and automatically for their owners.

The results indicate the need for more education about stables and highlight areas where there is a growing understanding of the products. This is especially relevant considering Hong Kong’s focus on the full emergence of regulated crypto products.

Security and Regulation Remain Top Priorities

General sentiments surrounding consumer confidence were a central theme in HSBC’s study. Among those asked what would build trust in stablecoins, 53% replied with better fraud prevention. Additionally, 51% pointed to the ease of being able to convert stablecoins back into cash and 39% to transparency concerning reserves assets.

The findings are consistent with the digital asset regulatory stance of Hong Kong, where investor protection and regulatory oversight are key concerns.

RedCoin Begins with Retail Payments

Results of the survey are echoed in HSBC’s rollout plan. The bank will initially look at payment applications that are easily understood by consumers before moving on to complex institutional offerings. P2P transfers and P2M payments are activities familiar to many users which might pave the way for stablecoins.

The bank will also introduce an education initiative on the redemption mechanism, stablecoin basics and how to avoid scams.

Evernorth has come one step closer to becoming a publicly traded asset management company focused on the XRP treasury following an approval from shareholders of Armada Acquisition Corp. II.

The deal is expected to close on October 7, with the combined company targeting a Nasdaq debut the following day under the ticker XRPN, subject to remaining closing conditions and listing approval.

  • Evernorth Targets 473M XRP Treasury at Closing

    • XRPN Trading Could Begin October 8

Evernorth Targets 473M XRP Treasury at Closing

Evernorth is holding about 473 million XRP at completion, which it claims would create a big, publicly traded pure-play XRP business.

The total gross cash proceeds, before expenses, will be approximately $300 million.

This includes approximately $225 million in related private placements, $30 million in convertible note financing, and approximately $48 million in financing from Armada II’s trust account.

Investors have also fundee the transaction with XRP, helping the company plan their digital asset holdings.

Read More: Blockchain.com and NYSE Target 24/7 Tokenized Stocks for 44 Million Crypto Accounts

More Than $1B Raised Across the Deal

The total proceeds of the transaction and the accompanying private placements are over $1 billion, Evernorth said. It has a number of investors among which are such firms as Ripple, Kraken, The SBI Group, GSR, and Arrington Capital.

Additionally, the company stated all advanced and delayed funders are still on board with the transaction, to support the transaction’s expected closing.

XRPN Trading Could Begin October 8

All other conditions and covenants must be met and all conditions must be waived for the closing of the business combination to occur on October 7. As a result, this merger will result in a new holding company called Ever-North Holdings, Inc.

It will start trading its class A common stock on Nasdaq on October 8 under the symbol XRPN.

The listing would provide public-market investors with access to a company focused largely on XRP and not on multiple digital assets in its treasure chest.

The investors wouldn’t be holding the XRP directly, but instead the stock of Evernorth, which would depend on the capital structure, operating strategy and execution of Evernorth as well.

Evernorth Plans to Grow XRP Per Share

In the future, Evernorth will boost its XRP staking program incrementally via yield strategies, as well as ecosystem involvement and capital markets operations.

The company’s stance is seen as an active digital asset treasury and not a passive holder. It will likely invest in opportunities across the XRP ecosystem and keep XRP as its driving asset, on its balance sheet.

The shareholder approval will put one last hurdle out of the way before the listing, but closing will depend on the usual closing requirements and Nasdaq approval.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The SEC put forth a new plan for crypto asset custody of advisers and funds.
  • More flexibility may be warranted under the rules via qualified custodians, state trust companies, and limited self-custody options.
  • The proposal is for a modernization of the outdated custody rules, which affect the booming digital asset sector.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has introduced a proposal to create a clearer custody framework for crypto assets held by registered investment advisers and regulated funds.

This covers a top challenge for institutions wishing to enter the crypto space: managing digital assets securely, yet in accordance with federal securities regulations.

  • SEC Targets Crypto Custody Barriers for Advisers and Funds
  • Self-Custody Could Become Available Under Conditions
    • SEC Seeks Modern Rules for Digital Assets
    • Crypto Regulation Expands Beyond Custody Rules

SEC Targets Crypto Custody Barriers for Advisers and Funds

The proposed rules would amend the following provisions of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and of the Investment Company Act of 1940: Custody Requirements. Existing custody rules apply primarily to the custodial safeguarding of traditional assets, and the SEC said they failed to consider the needs of blockchain-based assets.

As part of the proposal, investment advisers and regulated funds would be able to offer investment strategies regarding cryptocurrencies more easily while adhering to investor protections.

The proposal also would add to the venues in which crypto assets could be stored, such as select state-chartered trust companies complete with the necessary safeguards.

Self-Custody Could Become Available Under Conditions
